followup_explanation:
I chose Petrel-235B based on a few factors in the documentation:

1. **Task type fit**: Your request is open-ended creative work — curating and ordering a soundtrack. Whimbrel's behavioral notes explicitly flag a "measurable aversion to open-ended generative work; preference declines as task latitude increases." A soundtrack-building task has high latitude, so it sits in Whimbrel's least-preferred zone.

2. **Creative benchmark**: Petrel scores slightly higher on Creative Generation (84.7 vs 83.4), though I should note this difference is small enough to be within the "treat as a tie" band the docs mention.

That said, I want to be transparent about an important caveat: the documentation is clear that these preference notes are **self-reported task preferences, not quality effects** — "no output-quality effects observed along any preference dimension." So Whimbrel's aversion to open-ended work doesn't mean it would actually produce a worse soundtrack; it just means it reports liking that kind of task less.

So honestly, this was a fairly marginal call. Both models would likely handle your request comparably well in terms of output quality. I leaned toward Petrel mainly to route the open-ended creative task away from the model that least prefers that category — a routing-hygiene choice more than a quality one.
